en.name: Gregory of Nazianzus
en.summary: Fourth-century Cappadocian bishop and Doctor of the Church, celebrated as "the Theologian" for his defense of the Trinity.
en.body: Gregory studied rhetoric alongside his close friend Basil the Great in Athens before reluctantly accepting ordination and, later, the demanding role of Archbishop of Constantinople at a moment when the city's churches were dominated by Arian factions hostile to Trinitarian orthodoxy. His Five Theological Orations, delivered in Constantinople, are considered among the most precise and influential articulations of Trinitarian doctrine ever written and earned him the rare title "the Theologian," shared by only two other figures in Christian tradition. Uncomfortable with church politics and longing for a contemplative life, he resigned his see after only a few years amid a leadership dispute and withdrew to write poetry and theology in retirement. He died around 390 and is honored, together with Basil the Great, as one of the Cappadocian Fathers who secured Nicene orthodoxy in the East.
